hook: Water cuts the heat released when pyridine binds a zeolite acid site by about 150 kJ/mol.

readout.label: Less exothermic adsorption in water vs gas

summary: Water changes how strongly a base sticks to the acid sites of a zeolite catalyst. Calorimetry in water, combined with water-adsorption data in a thermodynamic cycle, links the liquid results to gas-phase values. The Si/Al trend seen in water comes from how much the water stabilizes the proton and pyridinium ion, not from acid strength. Only one zeolite framework and one probe base were tested.
title: Effect of Water on Elementary Reactions in Solid-Acid Catalyzed Reactions: Thermodynamics of Acid–Base Interactions in H-ZSM-5
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
